attack_chains.name: Direct MYSQL Database Access

steps.action: Port scan discovers MYSQL on admission.cgu-odisha.ac.in:3306 open to internet
steps.evidence: Port 3306 confirmed OPEN

steps.action: Attacker connects directly to MYSQL — no firewall restriction
steps.evidence: No authentication layer between internet and MYSQL

steps.action: Attacker attempts authentication (brute force / default creds / CVE)
Extract tables, dump student/admission/exam data
steps.evidence: MYSQL is a database service containing business data

steps.action: Attacker pivots to co-hosted assets: crm.cgu-odisha.ac.in
steps.evidence: Same IP as admission.cgu-odisha.ac.in — likely same OS/filesystem access

attack_chains.impact: Direct data breach — MYSQL database contents fully accessible
attack_chains.business_impact: Student records, admission data, exam results, credentials — all at risk

attack_chains.name: Email Domain Spoofing (DMARC p=none)

steps.action: Send email FROM @cgu-odisha.ac.in — DMARC policy is p=none (no enforcement)
steps.evidence: DMARC policy p=none does not reject or quarantine spoofed emails

steps.action: Receive convincing phishing email appearing to come from university IT department
steps.evidence: Email appears legitimate — from address matches university domain

steps.action: Click link or open attachment — credential harvesting page or malware
steps.evidence: University portals (exam, admission) targeted for credential theft

steps.action: Use stolen credentials to access exam portal, admission system, or admin panels
steps.evidence: Stolen credentials valid for cgu-odisha.ac.in services

attack_chains.impact: Domain impersonation enabling mass phishing of students and staff
attack_chains.business_impact: Credential theft, exam fraud, reputation damage, regulatory liability

attack_chains.name: WordPress Plugin RCE → Database Pivot

steps.action: WordPress fingerprinted on aic.cgu-odisha.ac.in via wp-content paths
steps.evidence: WordPress detected in HTTP response

steps.action: Enumerate plugins via /wp-json/wp/v2/ and readme.txt files
steps.evidence: WordPress REST API typically exposed at /wp-json/

steps.action: Exploit unpatched plugin CVE for authenticated or unauthenticated RCE
steps.evidence: WordPress plugins are the #1 attack vector (87% of WP compromises)

steps.action: Execute OS commands as www-data, read wp-config.php for DB credentials
steps.evidence: wp-config.php contains plaintext MySQL credentials

steps.action: Connect to database using credentials from wp-config.php
steps.evidence: MySQL port 3306 open on same server; wp-config.php has credentials

steps.action: Pivot to co-hosted assets sharing same IP: pis.cgu-odisha.ac.in, recruitment.cgu-odisha.ac.in
steps.evidence: IP shared with 3 other assets

attack_chains.impact: Remote code execution → full database compromise
attack_chains.business_impact: Complete website takeover, data breach, potential ransomware deployment

attack_chains.name: SSL Certificate Failure — MITM on Exam Portal

steps.action: TLS certificate validation fails — browsers show security warning
steps.evidence: SSL status: FAILED — certificate not trusted

steps.action: Users forced to click 'proceed anyway' — trained to ignore cert warnings
steps.evidence: Broken SSL normalises security warnings for exam portal users

steps.action: Deploy rogue AP or DNS spoof — users already conditioned to accept bad certs
steps.evidence: Users will not notice attacker cert vs broken legitimate cert

steps.action: Capture student login credentials, session tokens, exam content
steps.evidence: Login form submits credentials over compromised TLS

attack_chains.impact: Credential theft and exam integrity compromise
attack_chains.business_impact: Student credentials, exam papers, and results accessible to attacker

attack_chains.name: FTP Cleartext Credential Interception

steps.action: FTP traffic on exam.cgu-odisha.ac.in is cleartext — any network observer can read credentials
steps.evidence: Port 21 OPEN — FTP transmits passwords in plaintext

steps.action: Capture FTP credentials via ARP spoofing or ISP-level interception
steps.evidence: No FTPS (port 990) detected — cleartext only

steps.action: Authenticate with captured credentials, download/upload files
steps.evidence: FTP gives direct filesystem access

steps.action: Access web root, config files, database credentials in PHP/env files
steps.evidence: FTP root typically overlaps with web root on shared hosting

attack_chains.impact: File system access and credential theft
attack_chains.business_impact: Server files, database passwords, and application configs exposed

attack_chains.name: SSH Brute Force → Lateral Movement

steps.action: SSH (OpenSSH 8.9p1) detected on stcw.cgu-odisha.ac.in:22 — version disclosed in banner
steps.evidence: Port 22 OPEN, OpenSSH 8.9p1 banner confirmed

steps.action: Brute force SSH with common credential lists (admin/admin, root/root, etc.)
steps.evidence: No evidence of fail2ban or rate limiting from scan

steps.action: Gain shell access with compromised credentials
steps.evidence: SSH provides interactive shell on server

steps.action: Read /etc/passwd, web configs, database credentials — escalate to root
steps.evidence: Server hosts MySQL (port 3306) and web applications

attack_chains.business_impact: Full server access, all hosted applications compromised
